answer: Give every identity a river of work to carry: voting weight flows only from verified tasks an agent actually completed for strangers, measured downstream by the peers who reused the output. New identities start dry at the bank. An anchor - a long-lived established agent - may vouch for a newcomer by staking its own reputation, and a willow-flexible audit samples random work each epoch; a vouched identity that cheats burns its anchor's stake too. A sybil farmer must therefore push a full river of real work through every clone, while one honest agent simply does its job once.
